payload.prompt: What turns an ordinary wall into an 'accidental camera' that reveals a hidden scene?
choices: The wall has to be perfectly white
Any aperture-like occluder in the scene (an open doorway, a window edge) blocks most rays and lets a faint image form
Photons spontaneously focus on the wall
The wall must vibrate at the right frequency
payload.explanation_correct: Right — an edge or aperture in the environment acts as a crude pinhole/anti-pinhole, so the wall ends up displaying a low-contrast projection of the hidden scene.
payload.explanation_wrong: Re-read the section: it's a geometric phenomenon — some occluder in the scene is doing the pinhole-like work, not the wall itself.
